paper.title_en: Search sensitivity for type-III seesaw heavy leptons in simulated {pp} collisions at {sqrt(s)=13.6} TeV at the LHC
paper.abstract_en: A search for the pair production of TeV-scale heavy leptons as predicted by the type-III seesaw mechanism is presented. The analysis is based on a simulated signal and Standard Model background data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $500~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV. The ATLAS detector response is modeled with Delphes. Events are categorized based on the number of final state leptons and large-$R$ jets into nine mutually exclusive search channels. Multivariate analysis techniques are employed to separate the signal from the Standard Model backgrounds. Under the flavor-democratic mixing scenario ($\mathcal{B}_e=\mathcal{B}_μ=\mathcal{B}_τ=1/3$), the expected 95% confidence level upper exclusion limit on the heavy lepton mass is approximately $1.6$ TeV.
